title: Console metrics signal loss during SLO surge — diagnostic, hotpatch, and follow-ups
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a traffic surge tied to a customer rollout (Hosted tier), several tenants reported missing metrics and blank dashboard tiles. Traces appeared partially captured (trace gaps) and live panels showed stale values. This ticket tracks the triage, short-term mitigation (hotpatch), and permanent fixes.
observed_behavior: Between 2026-02-28 18:10 UTC and 2026-02-28 19:25 UTC, 4 tenants (including customer-123) reported >50% of dashboard tiles returning "no data". Trace linking failures observed where spans were present but not stitched to requests. Console live-panel latency spiked; ingestion pipeline reported partial tombstoning for metric shards.
impact_summary: Customer-facing dashboards blanked for multiple customers across Hosted and Dedicated. Several on-call escalations and a critical support ticket from a high-usage customer. Potential SLA exposure for Dedicated contracts if not remediated promptly.
hypothesis_and_root_cause: Initial hypothesis: aggressive autoscaler activity + short-lived KV cache eviction created an ingestion window where metrics were written to ephemeral shards that were later tombstoned by the indexer. Root cause: timing window mismatch between the ingest buffer retention policy and the shard consolidation job. When SLO surge occurred, consolidation ran before the write-ack window closed, producing orphaned metric documents and broken trace stitching keys.
short_term_mitigation: 1) Temporarily extend ingest-buffer retention from 30s -> 5m for affected tenants; 2) Pause shard consolidation job for 10 minutes while backfill runs; 3) Enable secondary ingestion fallback to event-log stream B for high-traffic tenants. These changes were applied as a hotpatch to avoid additional customer-visible loss.
long_term_plan: 1) Introduce coordination barrier between write-ack window and shard consolidation to guarantee idempotent consolidation; 2) Add deterministic tombstone reconciliation job that replays recent event logs to repair orphaned metrics; 3) Add unit + e2e tests that simulate SLO surge and ensure trace stitching across shard lifecycle; 4) Add console alert for "ingest-buffering-duration" anomalies.
decision_log: - 2026-03-01 02:10: Decided to apply temporary retention extension instead of immediate rollback to avoid global latency regression. (Decision by Aisha, Luca, Priya)
tradeoffs: Extending buffer retention increases memory/ephemeral storage costs and slightly increases warmup time for shards; acceptable as a temporary emergency measure. Permanent fix will focus on correctness without amplifying resource footprint.
implementation_notes: Hotpatch implemented in infra repo; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/9876. Changes: ingest_buffer retention param exposed as feature-flag, shard-consolidator pause endpoint, and fallback stream toggle. Console-side UX change to show 'ingest fallback' status added as well.
qa_and_validation: Post-hotpatch validation steps: 1) replayed customer-123 event window and confirmed dashboards populated; 2) synthetic surge test (k6) for 10 minutes at 3x normal traffic showed no metric tombstones; 3) trace re-stitch verification run produced >99.5% continuity across spans.
monitoring_and_rollout_plan: Step 1: Keep retention extension on for affected tenant groups for 48 hours while backfill completes. Step 2: Roll changes to 25% of tenants, observe ingest_buffer_duration and dashboard success rate for 30m. Step 3: Full rollout after green checks.
